accepted_examples.german: Der ganze Schnee auf dem Berg ist verschwunden.
accepted_examples.english: All the snow on the mountain has disappeared.
accepted_examples.note: Verschwunden is used predicatively and means disappeared; the English translation matches.

accepted_examples.german: Kann ich es wirklich zu diesem Preis haben?
accepted_examples.english: Can I really have it at this price?
accepted_examples.note: Preis means price in this sentence, and the English asks whether it can be bought at that price.

accepted_examples.german: Bitte sag mir, dass das ein Witz ist!
accepted_examples.english: Please tell me it's a joke.
accepted_examples.note: Witz is used in the ordinary sense joke; the translation matches.

accepted_examples.german: Hier ist alles vom Geist der Geschichte durchdrungen.
accepted_examples.english: Everything here is permeated by the spirit of history.
accepted_examples.note: Geist is used in the sense spirit; the sentence and translation agree.

accepted_examples.german: Ein alter Mann saß neben mir im Bus.
accepted_examples.english: An old man sat next to me on the bus.
accepted_examples.note: Neben expresses physical position beside the speaker; next to is an accurate translation.

accepted_examples.german: Die Firma gibt viel Geld für Werbung aus.
accepted_examples.english: The company spends a lot of money on advertising.
accepted_examples.note: Firma means company here; both sentence and translation are natural.

accepted_examples.german: Das Boot hielt sich dicht an der Küste.
accepted_examples.english: The boat hugged the shore.
accepted_examples.note: Boot means boat and the sentence is a clear, grammatically sound example.

accepted_examples.german: Die Katze hat angefangen, sich seltsam zu benehmen.
accepted_examples.english: The cat has started acting strangely.
accepted_examples.note: Seltsam is used adverbially with sich benehmen and means strangely.

accepted_examples.german: Tom fand den Brief, den Maria versteckt hatte.
accepted_examples.english: Tom found the letter Mary had hidden.
accepted_examples.note: Versteckt is the participial adjective hidden in the relative clause; the translation matches.

accepted_examples.german: Das Einzige, was wir fürchten müssen, ist die Furcht selbst.
accepted_examples.english: The only thing we have to fear is fear itself.
accepted_examples.note: Fürchten is used in its ordinary sense fear; this established quotation is translated accurately.

accepted_examples.german: Er hält sich gerade bei seiner Tante auf.
accepted_examples.english: He is staying with his aunt.
accepted_examples.note: Tante means aunt; the sentence and translation match.

accepted_examples.german: Nur aus Neugier gefragt, was erwarten Sie, was geschehen wird?
accepted_examples.english: Just out of curiosity, what do you expect to happen?
accepted_examples.note: Erwarten asks what someone expects to happen; the translation matches the entry sense.

accepted_examples.german: Ich kann auf ein Wunder hoffen, nicht wahr?
accepted_examples.english: I can hope for a miracle, can't I?
accepted_examples.note: Wunder means miracle and is used in that sense.

accepted_examples.german: Die Orange schmeckte weder süß noch sauer.
accepted_examples.english: The orange didn't taste either sweet or sour.
accepted_examples.note: Sauer means sour in the taste contrast; the translation is exact.

accepted_examples.german: Du bist vermutlich nicht in der Stimmung, das jetzt zu erfahren, aber ich muss dir etwas Wichtiges mitteilen.
accepted_examples.english: You may not be in the mood to hear this now, but I need to tell you something important.
accepted_examples.note: Vermutlich means probably/may and is used to express likelihood with uncertainty.

accepted_examples.german: Ein Major musste das Kommando über die Division übernehmen.
accepted_examples.english: A major had to take command of the division.
accepted_examples.note: Major is the military rank in the sentence; the English translation matches.

accepted_examples.german: Ich war damals jung und naiv.
accepted_examples.english: I was young and naive at that time.
accepted_examples.note: Jung describes the speaker as young; the translation is accurate.

accepted_examples.german: Ich fand, dass es mich älter aussehen ließ.
accepted_examples.english: I thought it made me look older.
accepted_examples.note: Aussehen means look/appear and is used as a bare infinitive after lassen.

accepted_examples.german: Ich schwöre, dass ich dich immer beschützen werde.
accepted_examples.english: I swear I'll always protect you.
accepted_examples.note: Beschützen is correctly used for protecting someone; the translation matches.

accepted_examples.german: Ich gratuliere! Sie haben eine Tochter geboren.
accepted_examples.english: Congratulations! You've given birth to a daughter.
accepted_examples.note: Gebären is represented by the participle geboren; the translation correctly says give birth.

held_examples.german: Tom süßte sich den Tee mit Honig statt mit Zucker; Maria süßte sich ihren gar nicht.
held_examples.reason: The candidate is an unwieldy two-person semicolon sentence with a difficult reflexive construction for a basic verb example.

held_examples.german: He! Was versteckst du da hinter deinem Rücken?
held_examples.reason: The interjection He! is unusual and distracting in a learner example; use a direct, current sentence.

held_examples.german: Dieses Fenster lässt sich nicht öffnen. Schau mal, ob du es gängig machen kannst.
held_examples.reason: The long sentence adds an uncommon phrase (gängig machen) and distracts from the basic meaning open.

held_examples.german: Tom hat es zu einem guten Preis verkauft.
held_examples.reason: The candidate uses verkauft as the main verb participle although this entry is the adjective sold; this replacement makes its predicative adjective use explicit.

editorial_examples.english: I sweeten my tea with honey.

editorial_examples.german: Ich habe mir den Rücken verletzt.

plural_reviews.note: Duden lists all three plural variants for the sofa sense.
plural_reviews.usage_note: All three forms are standard variants.

plural_reviews.note: For expression/term, the plural is Ausdrücke; Ausdrucke without umlaut is a different sense (printed copies).
plural_reviews.usage_note: Use Ausdrücke for expression/term; Ausdrucke belongs to the printing sense.

plural_reviews.note: The wheel sense forms Räder.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Standard plural: Räder.

plural_reviews.note: For a substantivized adjective meaning an adult, the nominative plural is Erwachsene; other cases may show Erwachsenen.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Nominative plural: Erwachsene; use Erwachsenen in weakly declined cases.

plural_reviews.note: For the female prisoner sense, the nominative plural is Gefangene; weakly declined cases use Gefangenen.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Nominative plural: Gefangene; use Gefangenen in weakly declined cases.

plural_reviews.note: Knarre forms Knarren; the slang register belongs to the meaning, not the plural.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Slang term for gun; standard plural Knarren.

plural_reviews.value: Usually singular as a collective in the employee/staff sense.
plural_reviews.note: Duden gives the collective staff sense and only singular declension; the extracted Personale is not a normal learner plural for this sense.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Collective noun normally used in the singular; use Beschäftigte or Mitarbeitende for individuals.

plural_reviews.note: For an officer, Duden lists Leutnants as the usual plural and Leutnante as rare; the rank itself can be used without plural.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Leutnants is usual for officers; Leutnante is rare. The rank title itself is often singular.

plural_reviews.note: Duden lists Bewusstseine and explicitly marks the plural rare.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Rare plural; the abstract concept is normally singular.

plural_reviews.note: Duden explicitly lists Beuten for the loot/prey sense.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Plural is Beuten; the collective sense is often singular.

plural_reviews.note: For the building/structure sense the plural is Bauten; Baue belongs to the animal-den sense.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Use Bauten for structures; Baue is a different sense (animal burrows).

plural_reviews.note: Duden marks Hitzen as a technical plural; everyday heat is normally singular.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Hitzen is technical; the ordinary heat sense is normally singular.

plural_reviews.note: Ferien is plural-only for holidays; no singular Ferien is used in this sense.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Plural-only noun.

plural_reviews.note: For the beer sense, Weiße is the nominative plural; Weißen is an inflected case form.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Nominative plural: Weiße; dative/weak forms may be Weißen.

plural_reviews.note: Duden lists Admirale as the usual plural and Admiräle as an alternative; the military rank title itself may be singular.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Admirale is usual; Admiräle is also correct.

plural_reviews.note: Puls forms Pulse.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Standard plural: Pulse.

plural_reviews.note: For the hallway sense, the plural is Flure.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Standard plural: Flure.

plural_reviews.note: Laster has an unchanged plural in the vice sense.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Plural is unchanged: Laster.

plural_reviews.note: Both Flecke and Flecken are used for spots/stains; Duden uses Flecke as the primary form and also records Flecken as a variant.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Flecke is the primary form; Flecken is also used.

plural_reviews.note: For substantivized Verdächtiger, the nominative plural is Verdächtige; weakly declined cases use Verdächtigen.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Nominative plural: Verdächtige; use Verdächtigen in weakly declined cases.

plural_reviews.note: Enkel has an unchanged plural.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Plural is unchanged: Enkel.

plural_reviews.note: Duden represents Sandwich[e]s and also lists Sandwiche for the food sense, covering Sandwiches, Sandwichs and Sandwiche.
plural_reviews.usage_note: All three variants are recorded; Sandwiches is a clear learner-facing form.

plural_reviews.note: Duden lists both Toaste and Toasts, including for the toast/salutation sense.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Both Toaste and Toasts are standard.

plural_reviews.note: Duden lists Coaches and Coachs for a trainer/coach.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Both Coaches and Coachs are standard.

plural_reviews.note: The countable personification/representative form can take Michels; Michel alone is not a distinct plural in ordinary use.
plural_reviews.usage_note: The cultural personification “der deutsche Michel” is usually singular; Michels is possible when counting individual figures.

plural_reviews.note: For a bloc/grouping, the plural is Blöcke; Blocks belongs to other meanings/loanword uses.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Use Blöcke for political or organizational blocs.

plural_reviews.value: Usually singular in this abstract fear/anxiety sense.
plural_reviews.note: Duden gives only singular declension for Furcht; the extracted Fürchte is not a normal plural in this abstract sense.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Usually singular; do not use Fürchte as the ordinary plural.

plural_reviews.note: Both Tempi and Tempos are accepted plurals for tempo/rate.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Both Tempi and Tempos are used.

plural_reviews.note: For the edge/border sense, the plural is Ränder.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Standard plural: Ränder.

plural_reviews.note: For the substantivized adjective meaning a rich person, the nominative plural is Reiche; weakly declined forms use Reichen.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Nominative plural: Reiche; use Reichen in weakly declined cases.
